strengths: Intuitive and well-motivated approach using convex primitives as an editable geometric interface for controllable image synthesis
Novel texture hint generation algorithm based on point cloud correspondences that effectively preserves object identity better than key-value transfer methods
Practical system design with no required fine-tuning of FLUX models and reasonable inference time (1-3 seconds for extraction, ~3 seconds for generation)
Comprehensive qualitative evaluation with extensive examples across multiple scales and editing types, demonstrating clear improvements over baselines (LooseControl, DragDiffusion)
Strong ablation studies showing advantages over existing texture preservation methods (Fig. 6) and detailed algorithmic descriptions for reproducibility
Honest and thorough documentation of failure cases and limitations (Fig. 9-10), providing valuable insights for future work
weaknesses: Limited quantitative evaluation: only ~48 test images with quantitative metrics and single main baseline (LooseControl); no quantitative comparison with other prominently discussed methods like DragDiffusion

Incremental technical novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (CDIS primitive decomposition + FLUX depth conditioning); texture hints are geometry-based warping + Voronoi inpainting, relatively straightforward

Significant unresolved limitations severely impact practical applicability: (1) large rotations (50°+) fail, (2) objects with holes cannot be reliably edited, (3) limited to generated images with specific noise tensors, (4) text-geometry conflicts produce artifacts, (5) no illumination/shadow modeling

Evaluation scope too narrow: test set ~48 images of relatively simple, well-composed scenes; limited evaluation on cluttered, occluded real-world scenarios; frequency of primitive decomposition failures not quantified

Primitive extraction bottleneck: method entirely depends on successful decomposition which can fail on cluttered scenes (Fig. 9); requires separate models for each K; domain gap between DepthAnythingv2 and in-the-wild data claimed as minimal but not empirically validated

Missing user studies for interactive system: claims intuitiveness but provides no user evaluation; no quantitative texture consistency metrics for multi-edit sequences (Fig. 8b shows visible artifacts)
Hyperparameter sensitivity concerns: numerous hyperparameters with ad-hoc tuning; multiple inpainting methods tried suggesting fragility; grid search described vaguely without sensitivity analysis
Reproducibility issues: depends on proprietary FLUX weights, DepthAnythingv2, 1.8M LAION training data; no code release mentioned; expensive to reproduce
Vague 'compositional generalization' claims: term not formally defined; unclear what aspects generalize and to what degree
Texture preservation imperfect on complex edits: Figure 8b demonstrates visible artifacts when composing multiple edits; acknowledged as not being 'tight' in such scenarios
